text:
Connor Brown came back from injury and New Jersey kept winning. The Devils are 9-1 in his last ten games, he has four goals in that stretch, and FOX Sports Radio New Jersey noted that the penalty kill has improved since his return.

The scoring won't hold at this rate. He's shooting 30.8% on 13 shots, four goals on 1.7 expected (the quality of his chances), and his typical range is closer to 12 to 17%. The Devils also have only 43% of the five-on-five chances with him on the ice, the worst relative mark on the team. He's a useful depth winger riding a hot stick and a hot team.

That still has value. He's 32, a sixth-round pick who has stuck for nearly 700 games, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking flagged a habit worth watching: 19% of his setups go across the royal road, the side-to-side pass goalies hate, against 7% for a typical forward. Our projection: about 17 goals.
